issues.description: The UML in the problem statement declares Pneumatic.raisePressure(pressureIncrease: int): void, but the solution's Pneumatic interface uses a double parameter (void raisePressure(double pressureIncrease)), while the solution's implementing classes (LaunchedDropdownTower, LaunchedRollerCoaster) implement raisePressure(int). This creates a parameter-type mismatch across artifacts and an internal inconsistency in the solution: the interface signature (double) does not match the implementations (int). This will confuse students about the correct parameter type to use (int vs double) and also causes the solution code to be non-compilable as provided.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the raisePressure parameter type consistent across all artifacts. Preferably align with the UML/problem statement and change the Pneumatic interface method signature to void raisePressure(int pressureIncrease) (update template and solution Pneumatic.java). Ensure all implementing classes use the same int parameter type and update their @Override methods accordingly. Alternatively, if double is intended, update the problem statement/UML and the implementations to use double consistently — but pick one type and make it consistent everywhere.
